results.title: Nebius Launches Live Spot GPU Pricing. Here’s What It Means for NBIS Stock.
results.author: Oleksandr Pylypenko
highlights:
Nebius Launches Live Spot GPU Pricing. Here’s What It Means for NBIS Stock.

# Nebius Launches Live Spot GPU Pricing. Here’s What It Means for NBIS Stock.

 Oleksandr Pylypenko Tue, October 27, 2026 at 7:30 AM EDT 7 min read

## Trading disclosure

...

Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading. Coinbase pays us for certain activity generated through this link. Prices displayed are informational.

...

The artificial intelligence (AI) boom has fueled extraordinary demand for computing power, putting companies that supply the infrastructure behind AI development in the spotlight. Among them is Nebius Group (NBIS), a fast-growing neocloud provider that has emerged as a notable beneficiary of the AI infrastructure spending surge. 

Now, Nebius is looking to build on that momentum with a new approach to selling its GPU computing capacity. The company recently announced live spot pricing, allowing customers to access GPU resources at prices that fluctuate with supply and demand rather than being limited to traditional purchasing options. The move marks an interesting development in Nebius's evolving business model as the company seeks to give customers greater flexibility in purchasing AI computing power.

...

## Nebius Moves Beyond Traditional GPU Contracts With Flexible Pricing 

Last Wednesday, Nebius announced that its GPU computing capacity is available at live spot pricing, allowing customers to track price changes and choose more flexible purchasing options. The move came after the company introduced dynamic spot pricing for preemptible virtual machines (VMs), which took effect on Oct. 8. 

Here is the new pricing structure: 

- Live spot pricing: The price for renting GPUs varies based on available capacity and customer demand, enabling customers to utilize discounted computing resources that can be interrupted. 
- Reserve auctions: Customers can reserve certain blocks of GPUs for shorter periods. 
- Pay-as-you-go: Customers can buy computing power on demand without a fixed-term reservation. 
- Capacity rebates: Nebius is piloting a program that allows customers to recover value by returning unused GPU capacity to the available pool. 

The company also announced plans to expand its AI Builder Program across Europe, including an additional $10 million in compute grants and further collaboration with Nvidia.

...

Nebius's new spot pricing mechanism could help address this issue by allowing the company to sell temporarily idle GPU capacity at rates determined by real-time supply and demand. For example, imagine that Nebius has GPU capacity available between larger customer workloads. Instead of allowing that capacity to sit idle, Nebius could offer it at discounted rates to smaller AI developers running experiments, processing data, or improving models. 

The approach is relatively similar to airlines offering discounted fares to fill seats that would otherwise remain empty. Notably, Nebius listed spot prices for Nvidia HGX B300 starting at $0.99 per GPU-hour as of Oct. 25, well below the effective on-demand rate of $9.50. While the discount is substantial, it comes with an important caveat: Nebius can reclaim spot instances with just 60 seconds' notice if the capacity is needed for on-demand customers.

results.title: This week, we announced spot pricing, and it’s a game changer for the market. The ultimate goal is to “sell the way the customer buys.” | Marc Boroditsky
results.author: Marc Boroditsky
highlights:
# This week, we announced spot pricing, and it’s a game changer for the market. The ultimate goal is to “sell the way the customer buys.” | Marc Boroditsky · LinkedIn · 2026-10-26T00:00:00+00:00

**Marc Boroditsky**.

---

This week, we announced spot pricing, and it’s a game changer for the market. The ultimate goal is to “sell the way the customer buys.”

Most GPU compute is still sold through private deals. If you’re a developer who needs a small amount of compute for a short time to test an idea, a weeks-long negotiation is not how you want to buy. It’s not how we want to sell, either.

Our spot price is set by real demand, never above on-demand, and anyone can see it at nebius.com/spot-prices. You set a max, and your job runs when the market is below it. It’s a real price, not one we made up.

Transparency leads to higher confidence and higher trust. That’s where partnerships start.

results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

results.title: Debt, not demand, will thin the neocloud herd · Rackline
highlights: Demand is not the problem. Lambda raised its 8×H100 rate from $2.99 per GPU-hour in January to $3.99 by April. RunPod said no data center GPU on its platform got cheaper between January and August, and Salad raises prices on most GPU classes Nov. 1. Amazon still lists an H100 hour at $6.88 and Microsoft at $12.29*, against $2.40 to $6.16* at the neoclouds. That is a shortage, not a glut.

highlights:
SAVRN· Oct 27, 2026 · 121 min read

...

On October 25, Elon Musk posted on X that SpaceX had closed $40 billion of debt for GPUs. He wrote that debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers, and that more than 200 neoclouds face death and consolidation. SiliconANGLE reported the post. SAVRN quoted it on October 26.

Our price data says something else. The SAVRN GPU same-item list index rose 6.1% from September 11 to October 26, on 117 prices. Of 182 GPU prices tracked across that stretch, 43 rose and 3 fell. Verda’s H100 on-demand rate went from $3.25 an hour to $4.56.

...

The models price in different units. Our tracker reads GPU clouds by the GPU-hour: neocloud H100 on-demand list prices run from $1.99 at Voltage Park to $6.155 for CoreWeave’s HGX H100, against $10.00 to $12.29 at Oracle, Google and Azure. Landlords price by the kilowatt-month. Full-stack contracts price by the megawatt-year. The table below sorts the 23 by model and by the buyers their filings or releases name.

...

- The Nebius letter says: Prices per megawatt are stepping up. From a $12 million 2026 base to more than $20 million in the second quarter and more than $40 million on short-term deals in the third. Post 168 also cites the letter’s more than 30% higher pricing on older GPUs in the second quarter than in the first.
- SAVRN tracks: Nebius raised its public list prices on October 21. HGX H100 on-demand went from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour (+16.9%), H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (+20.0%) and B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 (+18.9%). A B300 read of $9.50 against $7.85 is pending review. Nebius shares rose 17.2% from Oct 13, 2025 to Oct 23, 2026 (market quotes, post 168).
- Prepayments fund the build. Capex of $8,130.3 million in the half against $4,504.1 million of operating cash flow, most of it customer advances. The year-end contracted power target is 5 GW, with no basis stated; active power was about 170 MW at the end of 2025.
- From miner to Microsoft supplier. Operating AI Cloud capacity was about 40 MW at June 30. IREN targets 0.3 GW (IT) delivered in 2026 and 0.8 GW (IT) in 2027. The Microsoft GPUs are financed at a 6.0% weighted rate; a $2.4 billion financing for other customers carries 9.0% fixed.
- One buyer behind most of the book. The IPO sold 34,500,000 shares at $185.00 for $6.4 billion gross.

## Prices and scarcity

### GPU list prices rose 6.1% in six weeks.

On October 25, Elon Musk posted that SpaceX had closed $40 billion of debt for GPUs. He wrote that 200 or more neoclouds face what he called guppy-level death and consolidation. The SAVRN Index reads GPU list prices every day.

Our same-item GPU index was set at 100 on September 11, 2026, the day live checks began. It stood at 106.11 on October 26, up 6.1% on 117 list prices (SAVRN calculation). Of 182 GPU prices with readings at both ends, 43 rose and 3 fell (post 168). Verda moved its H100 on-demand rate from $3.25 to $4.56 an hour.

Among the neoclouds, Nebius and Crusoe raised list prices. CoreWeave, Lambda, Together AI, Vultr and Voltage Park did not move. Azure and Google left their tracked prices unchanged, and the hyperscalers’ standard H100 rates run about 2.5 to 2.7 times the typical price (post 168).

results.title: Are 200 Neoclouds About to Collapse? Our Data Says No
results.author: Chad Everett Harris
highlights:
The SAVRN Index tracks 229 GPU prices from 27 providers across 10 GPU types. 9 In addition, across all four markets we follow, it holds 797 prices from 55 providers. 10 For the GPU cloud market, we publish a same-item index of list prices. Because only items priced on both days count, a new product launch or an expiring discount cannot move it. 2 

Since September 11, that index has risen 6.1%. 2

...

Looking wider, we also followed every GPU price we could from mid-September through late October, including spot, serverless and reserved prices. Of 182 such prices, 43 rose while only 3 fell. 3 

The increases were not random. In particular, short-term and flexible prices moved first: spot, serverless, capacity blocks and monthly reservations. By contrast, one-year and three-year reserved prices did not move. That pattern is what you would expect if buyers who need capacity now are bidding for it.

One seller makes the point clearly, since Verda reprices its GPUs every few days. Its H100 on-demand price rose from $3.25 an hour on September 11 to $4.56 on October 25, an increase of 40%. 3 In fact, all 23 of the Verda prices we track went up.

Figure 2. Verda's published H100 on-demand price stepped up ten times in six weeks, with no cuts. Chart: SAVRN.

...

## The same H100, from $1.99 to $12.29

Here is the number that made me rethink this market. Our latest check found 31 standard on-demand prices for an NVIDIA H100. 3 The cheapest was $1.99 an hour, while the most expensive was $12.29. The median was $4.09. Our GPU page, which also counts calendar-mode and serverless rates, shows 38 on-demand prices with a typical price of $4.35. 9
